title: A failed night-panorama build permanently wedges the sky controller's pending guard
claim: createSkyController.use(): `pending = key; ... buildPanorama(...).then(apply)` (shared.js:178,194) has no .catch, and the NIGHT branch of buildPanorama (:137-149) awaits fetchBytes for the NITE IMG and its palette with no try/catch - unlike its day-sky sibling (:152-162), which catches and degrades to the gradient. On a rejected fetch, apply never runs, pending stays equal to that key, and every later use() for the same key returns at :177 (`key === pending`) - never retried, plus an unhandled rejection. Recovery only when a DIFFERENT key is requested (dawn). DFU reads local files and has no one-shot guard to wedge.
consequence: One failed NITE fetch at nightfall (lean data set, transient IndexedDB/network error) freezes the sky on the last day frame for the whole night with no retry.

title: Pickpocket 'found nothing valuable' uses the variant picker where DFU uses GetRandomText
claim: activate() passes `nothingText: () => randomVariant(FOUND_NOTHING_VALUABLE_TEXT_ID,...)` (townTalk.js:281-283) - a SubrecordSeparator-variant pick over plainText. C# PlayerActivate.cs:1645 uses TextProvider.GetRandomText(8999), pooling every Text TOKEN of the record (TextProvider.cs:250-269). The port built randomTextById for exactly this distinction and exposes it on this module (townTalk.js:679-681), but this site was not migrated. The two agree only if every 8999 variant is a single one-line token (unverifiable - no ARENA2 data here).
consequence: The no-gold pickpocket message draws from a differently-shaped pool than DFU's; a multi-line variant would print all its lines fused where DFU prints one.

title: %oth in the fallback question/answer chain uses the variant picker; DFU's Oath macro is GetRandomText
claim: expandRecord's oath (townTalk.js:168) and answerText's oath (:554) use `randomVariant(oathTextId(npcRace), '')`. C# resolves %oth via TalkManagerMCP.Oath() -> TextProvider.GetRandomText(201 + oathId) (TalkManagerMCP.cs:133-143), the flat token pool. The port's randomText accessor (:679-681) is documented as '%oth's seam' and the engine path consumes it (world.js:2303), but these two local sites stayed on randomVariant. textRsc.js:131-134 itself says the oath records hold 'several one-line oaths' in one record - the shape where the two pickers diverge. Scope: the pre-engine fallback paths, live in the ?exterior host (its createTownTalk passes no talkEngine, exterior.js:470-486).
consequence: In ?exterior, a greeting/question or where-is answer carrying %oth can render the whole oath list (or a mis-weighted pick) instead of one random oath line.

title: Steal mode says 'You are too far away' to an already-pickpocketed NPC; DFU is silent
claim: tryActivate gates steal distance before the attempted check (townTalk.js:269), with pickpocketAttempted tested only later inside activate() (:278). C# ActivateMobileNPC's Steal arm nests the distance test INSIDE `if (!mobileNpc.PickpocketByPlayerAttempted)` (PlayerActivate.cs:786-799), so an already-attempted NPC produces no output at any distance.
consequence: Activating an already-pickpocketed townsperson from beyond 3.2m in Steal mode prints a 'too far away' message DFU never shows.

title: Dungeon drowning deals zero damage: 3-arg call into the local 1-arg hurtPlayer wrapper
claim: breathTick's drowned arm calls hurtPlayer(playerEntity, playerEntity.health, { bypassShield: true }) (:2045), but the LOCAL hurtPlayer (:1030-1032) takes ONE arg (dmg) and forwards hurtEntity(playerEntity, dmg). So dmg = the playerEntity OBJECT; playerEntity.js:97's guard `if (!(dmg > 0)) return false` sees object>0 -> NaN -> false, and returns having done nothing. The call shape was copied from world.js:637 where hurtPlayer IS the 3-arg import (world.js:110); here the import is aliased hurtEntity (:26) and shadowed by the wrapper. The :2043 comment claims this exact bug class was already review-fixed.
consequence: PlayerEntity.cs:339-340 does SetHealth(0) at 0 breath; in the port a player out of breath underwater in a dungeon takes no damage at all - drowning can never hurt or kill. Only breathStep's unit test pins the systems half; no test pins this host call.

title: Runtime-spawned dungeon foes (rest encounters, quest CreateFoe) never get spell lists or a caster
claim: assignEnemySpells + EnemyCaster minting runs ONCE over the load-time foes array (:691-696). _spawnEncounter (:913-928) and spawnQuestFoe (:630-636) call buildFoeAt (:479), which never assigns spells; the frame loop's cast arm reads f.caster (:2312) - undefined for those foes. DFU's SetEnemyCareer assigns the spell lists on EVERY spawn (EnemyEntity.cs:350-386) and SetEnemySpells also pins magicka = 10*level+100 and four magic skills to 80 (:453-461); the port's makeEnemyEntity does neither. The port's own exterior pool assigns per-spawn inside its build path (exteriorFoes.js:107-109), so this host is the odd one out.
consequence: An Imp, Orc Shaman, Vampire, Lich, or CastsMagic class enemy spawned by a dungeon rest interruption or placed by a quest never casts a single spell and has no caster magicka pool; the same enemy at a load-time marker, or spawned outdoors, casts normally.
